### UPDATE 2026-11-22 JST — GLib 2.82.4 APC source and non-alertable cleanup audit PASS; zero monitor callback is not zero rebuild

- **Authoritative PR #62, branch-only diagnosis**: At the previously verified branch head `93174b0`, [original GLib 2.82.4 gio/gwin32appinfo.c](https://github.com/GNOME/glib/blob/2.82.4/gio/gwin32appinfo.c) and [gio/gwin32registrykey.c](https://github.com/GNOME/glib/blob/2.82.4/gio/gwin32registrykey.c) were obtained and inspected directly. `g_win32_registry_key_watch()` uses asynchronous `NtNotifyChangeMultipleKeys` with an **APC callback on the watch-registering thread**; its source comment specifies that APC dispatch needs the registering thread to enter an **alertable state**. An atomic compare-and-exchange prevents adding another watcher while the same key remains watched; `key_changed()` clears watch state and releases both its status block and the temporary key reference. `keys_updated()` re-arms watched keys, increments `gio_win32_appinfo_update_counter`, and schedules a worker job; the single-thread worker rebuilds, coalesces the counter, and signals waiters. `update_registry_data()` explicitly destroys previous app/handler/hash-table roots before constructing replacements; this is **not** proof that all referenced objects are freed, nor ownership proof for the 360B block.
- **Old probe post-cleanup APC confound confirmed by source**: [tests/gio_appinfo_key_handle_probe.c](https://github.com/taku077/c545d-recorder/blob/main/tests/gio_appinfo_key_handle_probe.c) deletes a disposable registry value with `RegDeleteValueW`, then ordinary **non-alertable** `Sleep(1200)`, enumeration and `after_cleanup257` census; later ordinary `Sleep(2500)`, context drain, enumeration and `settled_cleanup258` census. [Microsoft Sleep](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/synchapi/nf-synchapi-sleep) explicitly says use [SleepEx](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/synchapi/nf-synchapi-sleepex) for alertable waits. Thus the **single deferred registry parser pass at cycle258** in the original [Windows #44918598339](https://github.com/taku077/c545d-recorder/actions/runs/44918598339) is *consistent* with delayed delivery of a pending registry APC and subsequent asynchronous AppInfo worker scheduling. **APC dispatch timestamps were never captured; the actual cause remains a hypothesis, NOT a demonstrated APC firing time, event race, or native leak owner.** Do not silently relabel final cycle258 `settled_cleanup` as quiescent.
- **New extra finding about the original monitor counter**: The optional [tests/patch_glib_appinfo_monitor_worker_diagnostic.py](https://github.com/taku077/c545d-recorder/blob/main/tests/patch_glib_appinfo_monitor_worker_diagnostic.py) only invokes its worker-completion `g_app_info_monitor_fire()` when `C545D_DIAG_APPINFO_MONITOR_WORKER_FIRE` is set; the original 4-arm x256 CI [workflow](https://github.com/taku077/c545d-recorder/blob/main/.github/workflows/c545d-core-gio-msvc-native-cache-ab256-ci.yml) did **not** enable that flag. Consequently, the saved per-cycle `GAppInfoMonitor::changed` callback count zero cannot be used to infer that watched registry events, worker refreshes, or package enumerations were absent; indeed registry Combo had 258 parser summaries. Native spontaneous package monitor signal is a separate optional test path, not equivalent to the registry worker signal.
